title: Cisco ISE PassiveID — WMI / AD Agent / Syslog Provider Health
exclusions: Does not replace enterprise SIEM correlation for unrelated threat classes. Does not cover entities explicitly scoped out in operational_exceptions.csv. Pair with sibling UCs in the same subcategory when the SPL surface alone cannot prove control effectiveness (see prerequisiteUseCases on UC-17.1.45).
evidence: Saved search uc_17_1_45_cisco_ise_passiveid_wmi_ad_agent_syslog, dashboard panel tied to this UC, weekly CSV export archived to index=evidence with change-ticket reference, and git-tracked lookup baselines referenced in the search.

compliance.assurance_rationale: Art.21(2)(d) covers access control. PassiveID is the user-context source for NGFW access enforcement.
compliance.controlObjective: Maintain user-context source for downstream access enforcement.

compliance.assurance_rationale: A.8.20 (Networks security) — user-context fidelity is critical for network controls.
AC-4 (Information Flow Enforcement) — user-context driven flow enforcement requires PassiveID.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Stop the AD Agent service on a Domain Controller. Within 5 min ISE emits 91020 (AD Agent connection lost). UC-17.1.45 fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Restart the AD Agent. ISE reconnects. Alert clears.

dataSources: ISE syslog `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog` *PassiveID* category — codes `91000` (PassiveID provider connected), `91001` (provider disconnected), `91002` (provider error), `91003` (mapping ingested), `91010` (WMI session ended unexpectedly), `91020` (AD Agent connection lost), `91030` (syslog provider parse error). Field: `provider_type` (WMI/AD-Agent/syslog/SPAN/Endpoint/REST), `provider_name`, `mapping_count`. ISE OpenAPI `/api/v1/passiveid/providerstatus` polled every 5 min, written to `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:passiveid_health`.
spl:
(index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode IN (91000, 91001, 91002, 91010, 91020, 91030))
  OR (index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:passiveid_health")
| stats count latest(_time) as last_event count(eval(MessageCode=="91001")) as drops count(eval(MessageCode=="91002")) as errors latest(provider_status) as status by provider_type, provider_name
| where drops > 1 OR errors > 0 OR status=="DOWN"
| sort - errors - drops
description: Detects PassiveID provider failures (WMI, AD Agent, syslog, SPAN, Endpoint, REST). PassiveID is how ISE acquires user-to-IP mappings without 802.1X — critical for non-supplicant networks where the user identity comes from AD logon events.
value: PassiveID is the user-context backbone for many NGFW deployments — Cisco FTD/FMC, Cisco Secure Firewall, third-party firewalls all consume PassiveID-derived user-to-IP mappings via pxGrid or REST. When PassiveID providers fail, downstream firewall policies that gate by user identity revert to anonymous treatment.
implementation: Confirm *PassiveID* logging category at INFO. Deploy OpenAPI poller. Schedule every 5 min, search window `-15m@m to @m`, trigger on count > 0, throttle suppression on `provider_name` for 30 min.
visualization: (1) Single value: providers DOWN. (2) Per-provider mapping rate timechart. (3) Top-N providers with errors.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Planned change activity in the CMDB or change calendar produces expected deviations that match this detection pattern during approved maintenance. Cross-check ServiceNow change records for `state=implement` and the affected CI list.

2. **Backup and batch job cycles** — Nightly ETL, backup agents, or log rotation jobs generate bursts of similar events that resemble alert conditions but occur on a fixed schedule. Compare `_time` against the documented batch window before paging.

3. **Onboarding and provisioning bursts** — New users, devices, or services provisioned in bulk can temporarily skew counts until baselines stabilize. Filter events tagged `onboarding=true` in the identity or asset lookup.

4. **Monitoring and health-check traffic** — Synthetic transactions or internal scanner accounts generate probe traffic designed to exercise the control. Exclude service accounts listed in `monitoring_exceptions.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain a KV Store lookup `operational_exceptions.csv` with columns `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `approved_by`. Join the saved search to this lookup and filter `where isnull(exception_reason) OR now() > valid_until` so approved windows suppress alerts without muting the search globally.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• ISE PassiveID configured with at least one provider.
• `passiveid_providers.csv` with `provider_name`, `provider_type`, `is_critical`, `domain`.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable *PassiveID* category at INFO.

Step 2 — Create the search
Search in `spl` field. Schedule every 5 min.

Step 3 — Validate
Provoke as above.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard "ISE — PassiveID Health":
• Per-provider status tile.
• Mapping rate timechart.
• Top-N error sources.

Alerting: PagerDuty medium on provider DOWN.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **WMI fails** — DC's WMI namespace permission for ISE service account. PowerShell `wmic` test.
• **AD Agent missing** — installer not deployed on DC; deploy or update.
• **REST provider failures** — endpoint URL/cert/auth issue; validate from PSN CLI.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)).). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog, cisco:ise:passiveid_health into nac. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`drops, errors, provider_name, provider_type`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: When a person logs onto a Windows computer at the office, ISE learns who's using which IP address by listening to the company directory. We watch this listening line — if it goes silent, ISE no longer knows who's who, and other security tools that depend on that info also stop working.
